head: e41bdf639a299e4f83c1fe15605f5fe32deb0ba8
summary:
The slice matches the design. A finished whole-drive scan whose volume figure lands shows the panel under the unchanged coverage line. The panel gives:
- the $MFT's valid data length as the one measured part, used only when it is above 0 and no more than the unseen space;
- a remainder labelled as space this account cannot read, which says it includes the container layer store only when one was left out;
- the folders: the left-out store first, then at most 20 unreadable folders chosen shallowest first, then 'and N more'. The report keeps every folder, with no path.
- the files whose own size could not be read, kept apart from the unseen space.

No panel is shown for a folder root, a root that could not be read, a refused root, a stopped scan or an over-count. A mapped or other network root gets no figure at all. The five merged fixes are in:
- the store's words now come only from UnreadableRows, with one arm per reason and a neutral fallback;
- counts are written through FigureText.Count;
- the hook's FoldersIn now reads '1 folder';
- the UnreadableTab and UnreadableExpander comments are corrected.

What I ran myself:
- Whole suite: 1204/1204 passed.
- The App and the window hook build with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- Fitness op=check: all 105 rules hold, including the three SL-001 rules.
- tests/bugs/SL-001-WrittenOnceRules.Tests.ps1: all checks held.
- Window cases A, D and G on a freshly published exe: all held.
  - Case A: $MFT 10,540,285,952, equal to FileInfo of C:\$MFT; measured + remainder = unseen; panel top 113 px against 76 px shown.
  - Case D: two unreadable folders, no size, the remainder counts both.
  - Case G: the singular note and the singular panel text.

One major finding: the new always-on test EveryMappedNetworkDriveOnThisPcIsRemoteAndGetsNoFigure makes the default suite depend on this PC's persistent Z:\ mapping (\\100.109.48.75\collab) being reachable. It fails, or waits the full 45 s and times out, whenever that server is down. It is not behind an opt-in trait, and the opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK fact the design planned for this check was never written. There are also two minor stale comments (text).

Second reader, for inputs: Input pass over the slice's new readers, matchers and native paths. I built and ran a temporary xUnit probe, then deleted it. I also checked that the tree is back to its earlier status and no SUBST letter is left.

What I ran:
- A SUBST letter over the mapped Z:\ (the 'SUBST over a network path' alias, which no existing test feeds in): Kernel32.IsRemoteRoot answered true and VolumeSpace.Read gave no figure.
- A SUBST letter over D:\: TryGetMftValidData gave D:'s own $MFT, 89,15,51,744, equal to FileInfo('D:\$MFT'). C: gave its own figure, IsRemoteRoot answered false, and the used read answered D's volume.
- A lower-case root (c:\): remote false, and the $MFT read works.
- The hook's CountersReading.FoldersIn, reading back what FigureText.Counters writes at counts of 0, 1, 2, 4,022 and 1,234,567 under fr-FR (U+202F group separator), de-DE, de-CH (’), en-IN (12,34,567), ar-SA and fa-IR (U+066C). It read every count correctly, including '1 folder' followed by '1 folder unreadable'.
- The three new fitness entries, parsed with the engine venv's PyYAML: the plain scalars come out byte-for-byte as the corpus script's own reader takes them, and Python re agrees with .NET on the spellings I tried.

What I read:
- The bound/thread answer order of the two completion sources: every interleaving leaves the figure null, or a number with the $MFT task already complete. The App never waits on it.
- ShallowestFirst and Depth: rows are full display paths, the root row is depth 0, the cap boundary at 20 and 21 is handled, and the rows come back in path order.
- UnreadableRows.Build cannot produce duplicate rows: FolderDone adds each folder at most once, so folders[] and core.unreadable agree.
- The new name-clash checker: no x:Name in MainWindow.xaml is a Core type name, and MainWindow has no generic methods. Its spelling gaps (bare Name=, single quotes, generic methods, Core types) are hypothetical in this tree, and each leads to a compile error anyway.

One input family is left open, an extra rather than a defect. The plural tripwire matches only an upper-case ':N0' followed by a lower-case noun. It is quiet on '{n} files', on '{n:n0} files' (the same .NET format in lower case) and on '{n:N0} Files'. Each of these writes '1 files', the SC-044 defect it exists to stop.

findings.claim:
EveryMappedNetworkDriveOnThisPcIsRemoteAndGetsNoFigure runs in the default suite with no opt-in trait, and opens the root of every DriveType.Network letter.

This PC's Z:\ is a persistent mapping to \\100.109.48.75\collab. Win32_NetworkConnection shows Persistent=True, and a remembered connection keeps DriveType Network while its server is unreachable. When the server is down:
- either IsRemoteRoot's open fails, it returns null, and Assert.True(remote) fails;
- or the open blocks past FigureWait (45 s), and WaitAsync throws TimeoutException. That wait is paid twice, once for IsRemoteRoot and once for Read.

So `eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx`, the gate every later stage runs, goes red on this PC for a reason that has nothing to do with the code. The test's own summary claims 'A share that stopped answering cannot hold the test past its bound', but its assertions turn exactly that case red.

The project keeps network-touching tests behind opt-in traits (Network=SMB-LOOPBACK, Network=TEST-NET-1 in FsaDefaultTestFilter). The design planned an opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK fact, AMappedLoopbackShareGetsNoFigure, for this real-redirector branch. O-020, the always-on Z:\ probe, was waived.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/VolumeUsageTests.cs:586-600. Win32_NetworkConnection on this PC: Z: \\100.109.48.75\collab, Connected, Persistent True. FigureWait = 45 s (VolumeUsageTests.cs:27). FsaDefaultTestFilter is in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj:13.

quote.text: Assert.True(remote, $"{root} is a network drive and its root handle did not say so");

findings.fix:
Either option fixes it:
- Assert `Assert.NotEqual(false, remote)` together with `Assert.Null(figure)`. A share that cannot be asked also gets no figure, which is the production contract. Catch the TimeoutException as the same 'could not tell' outcome.
- Or put the fact behind an opt-in trait with a matching FsaDefaultTestFilter clause, as the project does for every other network-touching test, or write the design's opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK AMappedLoopbackShareGetsNoFigure instead.

findings.claim:
The public VolumeUsedMft doc says it is 'always null when VolumeUsed is'. One interleaving breaks that:
1. The read returns as the bound passes.
2. The thread's mft.TrySetResult(size) wins.
3. The bound's continuation then fails on mft but wins figure.TrySetResult(null).
4. The thread's figure.TrySetResult(used) is dropped.
The result is VolumeUsed = null with VolumeUsedMft = size. The guarantee the window relies on, that VolumeUsedMft is complete whenever VolumeUsed completes with a number, does hold.
findings.evidence: VolumeSpace.Answer sets mft, then figure. The Task.Delay bound continuation sets mft null, then figure null, with no lock between the two pairs (src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/VolumeSpace.cs:62-69, :127-128).

quote.text: /// read's bound passed; always null when <see cref="VolumeUsed"/> is.

findings.fix: Reword to 'null whenever VolumeUsed is null, except when the read lands just as its bound passes; complete whenever VolumeUsed has completed with a number'.

findings.claim: The counters-line comments credit the counters line to SL-044. SL-044 is the folder-tree slice (WindowCases.ps1:57 'T-001 to T-006 (SL-044) are the folder tree'). This fix is SC-044, built in SL-001. The same wrong reference is in CountersReadingTests.cs:6, CountersReading.cs:6 and the Core.Tests csproj link comment.

quote.text: /// The scanning panel's counters line (SL-044): files, folders, size and size on disk, and the folders that could not be read

findings.fix: Replace '(SL-044)' with '(SC-044, SL-001)' in these comments.

findings.claim: The new tripwire 'no count in the App is written with a fixed plural' only recognises a count formatted with an upper-case ':N0' and followed by a lower-case noun. It stays quiet on three ordinary ways to write the same defect, each of which puts '1 files' / '1 folders' on screen (SC-044). (1) '$"{n} files"', with no format specifier, the plainest C# spelling. (2) '$"{n:n0} files"': .NET format specifiers ignore case, so 'n0' is the same N0 format. (3) '$"{n:N0} Files were deleted"', with the noun capitalised at the start of a sentence, because the pattern has no (?i). The 'because' text declares as gaps ToString("N0") + " files", other format strings and other nouns. It does not name these three, and two of them are not 'other format strings' at all. Confirmed by running the pattern in both .NET [regex] and the engine's Python re (read through PyYAML from .taad/fitness.yaml): all three return False, while '{n:N0} files' returns True.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml, entry 'no count in the App is written with a fixed plural', must_not_match '\{[^{}\r\n]*:N0\}\s*(?:files|folders|links)\b'. Measured on these rows: '{n} files' False, '{n:n0} files' False, '{n:N0} Files' False, '{n:N0} files' True (PyYAML plus re.search, and .NET Regex.IsMatch). The widened form below has 0 hits over every src/FsAnalyser.App/**/*.cs file, stays quiet on the corpus's quiet rows Q9 to Q14 (Count(...), the 'of' figure, FigureText's '{n:N0} {noun}s', the bracketed count, 'Top N of', and FormatSize's '{bytes:N0} bytes'), and still fires on P1 to P6.
findings.fix: Replace the pattern with '(?i)\{[^{}\r\n]*\}\s*(?:files|folders|links)\b', so any interpolation hole followed by one of the plural nouns fires, whatever its format and case. Add must-fire rows to tests/bugs/SL-001-WrittenOnceRules.Tests.ps1: '$"{n} files"', '$"{n:n0} folders"' and '$"{n:N0} Files were deleted"'. The existing quiet rows stay quiet under the new pattern (measured).
findings.class_of: count-with-fixed-plural spellings the plural tripwire misses

obligations.evidence: VolumeSpace.Start answers both sources null for a root that is not a drive root (VolumeSpace.cs:53-58). AddVolumeInUse then draws no panel, and ShowOutcome has already called HideCoverage (MainWindow.xaml.cs:603). Case B in SL-001-CoveragePanel.Tests.ps1 asserts coverage null and top null. Ran by the builder, not by me.

ShowProblem calls HideCoverage (MainWindow.xaml.cs:910). IsRemoteRoot returns null when the open fails, and Read then gives null. VolumeUsageTests.ADriveLetterWithNothingBehindItCannotBeAsked passed in my suite run.

CoveragePanelText.Build returns null when !finished (CoveragePanelText.cs:81), and AddVolumeInUse passes detail.Finished. Every Stopped ending reaches it with Finished=false. Case H (a 24,000-folder SUBST tree, hook stop at 15 folders) and CoveragePanelTextTests.AScanThatDidNotFinishHasNoPanel cover it. Case H was run by the builder; the unit test passed in my run.
Build has `if (!finished || unseen < 0) return null;`. CoveragePanelTextTests.AScanThatCountedMoreThanTheVolumeReportsHasNoPanel passed.

IncludesStore = facts.NotScanned.Count > 0, and the remainder appends UnreadableRows.NotScannedInRemainder (CoveragePanelText.cs:92-98). Folders put the not-scanned entry first. Case E (real store, precaution on) asserts skippedStores 1, opensUnderExcludedStore 0 and includesStore true. Ran by the builder; I did not re-run E.
CoveragePanelTextTests.TheRemainderNamesTheContainerLayerStoreIfAndOnlyIfOneWasLeftOut feeds facts with no NotScanned rows. My case A run shows includesStore false and no container-layer wording.

Kernel32.TryGetMftValidData goes through the root handle's final path, then GetVolumePathNameW, then GetFileAttributesExW(<volume>$MFT). VolumeUsageTests.TheMftFigureOfASubstLetterIsTheVolumeUnderIt, with a 10-byte decoy named $MFT, passed in my suite run. Case A, re-run, shows the measured $MFT equal to FileInfo.

Build uses the $MFT only when 0 < mft <= unseen (CoveragePanelText.cs:85). The theory covers null, 0, -5, equal to unseen and above unseen. VolumeSpace.Answer catches a throwing mft probe and still answers the used figure; the test for that passed. Not exercised: the NTFS gate in Kernel32 against a real non-NTFS volume (no rig here).

SizeNotRead.OnDisk sums ChargedOnDisk over ProbeFailed files. SizeNotReadTests passed: two denied 64 KiB files give 128 KiB, inside Totals.BytesOnDisk, and a clean tree gives 0. My case G run: sizeNotRead {1, 65536}, unseen = volumeInUse - core.bytesOnDisk.

FigureText.Counters goes through Count. ProbeFailuresNote and VanishedNote go through Count, with its/their for 1. CountersReading.FoldersIn searches for ' folder'. CountersReadingTests and the CoveragePanelTextTests note theories passed. My case G run shows the singular note and the singular panel text.

VolumeSpace.Read gives a figure only when isRemote(root) is false (VolumeSpace.cs:91-92). IsRemoteRoot answers remote on FileRemoteProtocolInfo or a \\?\UNC\ final path. ARemoteRootGetsNoFigure passed, and so did the real-Z:\ fact, with Z: connected at the time. That fact is the M1 finding: it fails whenever the share is offline.

UnreadableRows now holds every store word: NotScannedText, NotScannedShortText, NotScannedNote, RefusedText and NotScannedInRemainder, each with one named arm and a neutral fallback, plus FlaggedReason. Grep shows no store word in any other App .cs file outside comments. The SL-001 fitness rule holds (Fitness check). UnreadableStoreWordsTests passed.

Owed to validate-slice. The code keeps the panel honest whichever way the precondition falls: the $MFT is a measured part only when it is no more than the unseen space (CoveragePanelText.cs:85). Whether the unseen space on the real C:\ is at least the $MFT is the spike's clause (b). Deciding it needs the person-allowed whole-C:\ scan, which nobody has run.

ScreenLines puts the heading and the measured, remainder and size-not-read lines first. Then come the store rows, then ShallowestFirst(Unreadable, 20) (fewest separators, ties in path order, shown in path order), then '  and N more folders, in the Unreadable folders tab' through Count. The remainder text counts every unreadable folder and never says 'above'. CoveragePanelTextTests.ManyDeepFoldersNeverCrowdOutTheShallowOnesAHumanRecognises passed.

WindowReport writes CoveragePanel.top as TranslatePoint inside OutcomeTextsContent, null unless IsVisible, and adds OutcomeTexts.verticalOffset. My case A run: top 113.08 against actualHeight 76, offset 0, a scroll away.

The model property is CoverageModel (MainWindow.xaml.cs), beside the static Coverage(...) method. The class is CoveragePanelText; the x:Names are CoveragePanel and CoverageLines. The App builds cleanly. MainWindowNameClashTests passed over the corpus and the real MainWindow.

Kernel32.OpenRootForQuery is the one CreateFile for these root queries: FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES, FILE_SHARE_ALL, OPEN_EXISTING, FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS. IsRemoteRoot and TryGetMftValidData both use it. FailCriticalErrorsTests counts the CreateFile sites and passed.

Waived, but built anyway as the always-on EveryMappedNetworkDriveOnThisPcIsRemoteAndGetsNoFigure (VolumeUsageTests.cs:586). It passed with Z: connected. As written, it makes the default suite depend on the share (finding M1).

cases.evidence: The named E001-1 and E001-5 scripts are not in the tree. Case A of tests/window/SL-001-CoveragePanel.Tests.ps1 is the stand-in. It takes a SUBST letter over a %TEMP% tree of 20 files, scans it as a finished whole drive, and checks the coverage fields, CoveragePanel visible and top, and the four OutcomeDetail lines. I re-ran it: all held.
Case B scans the same kind of tree by its folder path and asserts coverage null, CoveragePanel not visible and top null.

Case C scans Get-FreeDriveLetter + ':\' and asserts root-unreadable and coverage null. VolumeUsageTests.ADriveLetterWithNothingBehindItCannotBeAsked shows IsRemoteRoot null and Read null on a free letter.

Case H uses a 24,000-folder SUBST tree, which is local, so the volume figure lands. FSA_HOOK_MODE=stop and FSA_HOOK_AT_FOLDERS=15 stop it. It asserts outcome cancelled, coverage null, top null and the partial line word for word.
CoveragePanelTextTests.AScanThatCountedMoreThanTheVolumeReportsHasNoPanel feeds seenOnDisk above volumeInUse, including by 1 byte. No window rig can make an over-count.
Case D: two folders with icacls deny RD under the SUBST root. It asserts two 'unreadable' entries, both with a null size, equal to core.unreadable. I re-ran it: held.

Case E: a SUBST letter over the real %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers with the default precaution on. It asserts skippedStores 1, opensUnderExcludedStore 0, one not-scanned entry with no size, includesStore true and the store wording. Ran by the builder.
CoveragePanelTextTests feeds facts with no NotScanned rows and with only unreadable rows, and asserts includesStore false and no 'container layer'. Case A's tree has no store.

VolumeUsageTests.TheMftFigureOfASubstLetterIsTheVolumeUnderIt plants a 10-byte $MFT decoy in the SUBST target and asserts that the figure through the letter is above 1 MiB and within 64 MiB of C:\$MFT. This really feeds the 'reachable only through the final path' shape.

The Build theory feeds mft null, 0, -5, equal to unseen and above unseen. AThrowingMftProbeLeavesTheMftNullAndStillAnswersTheUsedFigure feeds a throwing probe. The non-NTFS shape reaches Build only as mft null. Kernel32's NTFS gate is never fed a real non-NTFS volume.

SizeNotReadTests denies 0x100080 (SYNCHRONIZE | FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES) on two 64 KiB files and has a clean tree. Cases F and G deny S,RA through icacls. I re-ran G: sizeNotRead {1, 65536}, unseen unchanged.

CountersReadingTests pins Counters(1,1,0,0,1) = '1 file, 1 folder, ..., 1 folder unreadable' and has FoldersIn read 1 and 4022. The note theories use n=1, 2, 40 and n=1, 2, 7. Case G checks the singular note in the real window.

ARemoteRootGetsNoFigure feeds isRemote true and null and asserts the used probe is never called. EveryMappedNetworkDriveOnThisPcIsRemoteAndGetsNoFigure asks the real Z:\ (see M1). A DFS letter and a SUBST over a network path are never fed; only IsUncFinalPath's string theory covers that form.

UnreadableStoreWordsTests feeds (NotScannedReason)9999 and (ScanRefusal)9999 to every function and enumerates Enum.GetValues. SL-001-WrittenOnceRules.Tests.ps1 runs the must-fire rows, which include today's five hand-typed copies, and the real tree. I ran it: all held.

drift: The design's filed_for_later names a new opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK fact, VolumeUsageTests.AMappedLoopbackShareGetsNoFigure (trait Network=SMB-LOOPBACK, already in FsaDefaultTestFilter), for the real-redirector branch. It was not written. In its place is an always-on default-suite probe of this PC's real Z:\. The build declared that probe as replacing the waived O-020 fact, not this one.

The remainder text contains the word 'measured' ('..., and it is not measured.'), but the CoveragePanelText component in the design says it 'never contains the word measured'. It satisfies the design's contract regex (?i)(?<!not |never )\bmeasured\b, which is what E001-3 is said to apply. A stricter planted check would fail on it.
